_meta.description: Section-role table for Step 3 v2.4. Deterministic classification of every H2-H4 heading (and non-first H1s) against section_roles; appendix modeled as a structural container, not a role; no LLM in the pipeline. A heading that matches nothing may take its parent's role, or the role its subsections unanimously matched (see matching_rule.parent_inheritance and matching_rule.child_consensus); every other outcome depends on the heading alone. Companion to step3_spec_v2.4.md, which is authoritative for process, persistence, and invariants.

structural_contract.note: Fixed mapping per Mathpix markdown convention. Levels are never inferred from heading frequency. Every H2-H4 heading becomes exactly one SectionNode (zero-silent-loss invariant, spec section 10).

matching_rule.pipeline: normalize (lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip trailing ':' '.') -> strip identifiers (numeric '2.1', alphabetic 'A.', Roman 'IV.', 'Section 4:') -> appendix-container parse -> exact match on semantic_heading, else whole-word phrase scan -> count DISTINCT ROLES among hits

outcomes.1_distinct_role: primary_role = that role; classification_status = resolved; classification_method = rule
outcomes.2plus_distinct_roles: primary_role = null; unresolved; candidate_roles recorded; ReviewTask(multi_role_match)

matching_rule.distinct_role_counting: Ambiguity is counted in roles, never keywords. Multiple keyword hits within one role ('prior research and extant literature' -> literature_review twice) = 1 distinct role = resolved, no task.
matching_rule.no_tie_breaking: Longest-phrase-wins does not exist in this version. Load-bearing ordering: exact match runs BEFORE the phrase scan and resolves immediately -- 'Summary and Conclusions' and 'Background literature' are literal keywords (conclusion, literature_review) and therefore resolve cleanly, never reaching distinct-role counting. Genuine multi_role_match cases are non-exact headings whose phrase hits span roles, e.g. 'Theoretical background and hypotheses derivation' (theory + introduction) or 'Background and literature review' (introduction + literature_review). Verified against this table.
matching_rule.parent_inheritance: A heading that produces 0 distinct roles takes its PARENT's role, recorded as classification_method = inherited. Four limits, each load-bearing: (a) never overrides a heading that matched -- direct evidence outranks positional evidence; (b) never overrides a 2+ distinct-role tie -- a tie is a real question with a real shortlist, and burying it would discard the best information the reviewer has; (c) never inherits from an unresolved parent -- a guess must not descend from a guess; (d) never inherits from the document_title node, which has no role by design, so sitting directly beneath the title yields no information. Where no limit applies the node stays unresolved and raises ReviewTask(zero_role_match). There is still no parent-context WEIGHTING and no LLM: inheritance is a fallback applied after the role table has spoken, never an input to it.
matching_rule.child_consensus: A heading that produces 0 distinct roles, and could not inherit downward, takes the role that EVERY one of its direct children independently matched. Recorded as classification_method = child_consensus, distinct from inherited because the evidence runs the other way and the two are different claims. Five limits: (a) never overrides a heading that matched; (b) never overrides a 2+ distinct-role tie -- subsections that disagree are the strongest reason to involve a person, not the moment to decide without one; (c) UNANIMOUS, never a majority; (d) at least TWO children, since one child is a data point that happens to be nested, not an agreement; (e) only children whose own method is 'rule' count, and Unknown never counts. Limit (e) is the justification, not a detail: consensus is evidence only because each child read its role off its own heading, independently. A child that inherited its role is an echo rather than a second opinion, so the rule fires at most once per node and never chains.

_meta.deferred_llm_design: The two-function LLM design (constrained candidate disambiguation for multi-role hits; contextual plausibility for zero-match H3/H4 against a reliable resolved ancestor), including its model/prompt provenance contract and strict output-validation/retry contract, is deferred out of MVP in full. It is preserved as deferred item 1 in step3_spec_v2.md section 13 and re-enters only if review-task volume becomes operationally excessive. No field in this table references it.
changelog_from_1.1: Appendix removed from section_roles entirely; re-modeled as structural_containers.appendix with prefix parsing ('Appendix B: X' -> container + label + semantic_heading) and bare-container behavior (primary_role = Unknown, no ReviewTask)
All LLM machinery removed: llm_plausibility_check block deleted; context_assigned status, classification_method=llm, resolved_via_parent_role no longer exist

Matching outcome for zero-match and multi-role headings changed from 'Unknown' to primary_role = null + unresolved + ReviewTask; the synthetic Unknown role is now reserved for the no-headings whole-document node and bare structural containers only
Distinct-role counting made explicit: same-role multi-keyword hits are not ambiguity
Identifier stripping extended: alphabetic ('A.') and Roman ('IV.') prefixes now stripped alongside numeric and 'Section N:' forms
Longest-phrase-wins deleted (was in the pre-1.1 full design and under consideration); 2+ distinct roles always -> review at MVP

G2 alias set added: container aliases (supporting information, supplementary material(s), supplementary information, online appendix, electronic supplementary material) and role aliases (credit authorship contribution statement -> author_contributions; competing interest / declaration of competing interest(s) -> conflict_of_interest)
content_class four-way split (analytical / citation_source / compliance_disclosure / administrative) unchanged from 1.1
Empty-body headings now classify normally from heading text (1.1 tagged them unresolved)

Preamble no longer produces a node: the 1.1 Title_and_front_matter synthetic role is removed entirely. Pre-heading text remains unsegmented in approved_markdown per the G1 ruling (MVP segments only explicit supported headings); zero-loss counts detected headings only, and the Data Availability-in-preamble case now lives in raw markdown outside every node (spec section 12)

No eval harness, gold corpus, or CI accuracy gate exists in this specification: demo.md is a reference test fixture only (spec section 15); the runtime zero-silent-loss invariant is the sole hard gate

Effective document-title overlay added (spec section 8): a human title ReviewDecision overrides the run's machine title determination at read time; SegmentationRun's stored title fields are never mutated, and reviewer_confirmed/human exist only as effective values

_meta.verification: Verified 13 Aug 2026 at 2.1 (22 SectionNodes, 6 ReviewTasks, 27/27 assertions). Re-verified 14 Aug 2026 at 2.2: same 22 nodes, 5 ReviewTasks, the sixth resolved because 4.2 Structural model inherits results from its parent. UNCHANGED at 2.3, and deliberately so: this fixture's one multi_role_match heading is the parent of its four zero_role_match ones, so a consensus rule that respects limits (a) and (b) has nothing to do here. A test asserts that rather than leaving it to be noticed later. The fixture is regenerated from the spec, never snapshotted from the implementation. UNCHANGED again at 2.4: the removed keyword appears in no demo.md heading, so the fixture's 22 nodes and 5 tasks are untouched.
changelog_from_2.0: Metadata only. No keyword, role, container or matching-rule change.
Version aligned with spec 2.1 (clarification amendments; structural contract unchanged).
Recorded the verification result and the machine-readable reference fixture.
structural_rule_version persisted on SegmentationRun remains "2.0": the H1-H4 structural contract did not change in 2.1.
changelog_from_2.1: First version whose changes alter classifications, and therefore the first to bump structural_rule_version, which stayed "2.0" through the whole of 2.1.

matching_rule.parent_independence replaced by matching_rule.parent_inheritance: a zero-match heading takes its parent's role, with four limits (no override of a match, no override of a tie, no inheritance from an unresolved parent, no inheritance from the document title).
classification_method gains "inherited", stored distinctly from "rule" so a role guessed from position stays countable and auditable against a role read from the heading itself.

structural_containers.appendix gains unmatched_suffix_behavior: an appendix whose suffix matches no role resolves to Unknown structurally instead of raising a question, matching what a bare 'Appendix B' already did. The suffix is still recorded in semantic_heading, so nothing is lost by not asking.
methodology keywords gain the singular "variable" alongside "variables", so '4.2 Dependent variable' classifies from its own heading rather than by inheritance. 156 keywords becomes 157.
changelog_from_2.2: matching_rule.child_consensus added: an unresolved heading may take the role its subsections unanimously matched, with five limits.
classification_method gains "child_consensus", stored separately from "inherited" because the evidence runs the opposite way and the two are different claims about the section.

Reference fixture unchanged. On the ESG paper the effect is one node: 5 EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS resolves to results from 5.1 Regression results, 5.2 and 5.3 Robustness checks, taking that paper to zero open questions.

No keyword, role or container change. "empirical analysis" was considered as a results keyword and REJECTED: the table already splits empirical strategy/approach (methodology) from empirical results/findings (results), so the phrase sits between them and its meaning depends on the paper. Reading the subsections reads the document; adding the keyword would guess on every future one.
changelog_from_2.3: "boundary conditions" REMOVED from results. It classified "4.5 RESEARCH FIELD AND BOUNDARY CONDITIONS" as results inside a methodology section; the phrase is far more common in theory and methodology, so as a results keyword it was miscategorised. 157 keywords becomes 156.

What the removal does NOT do: that heading does not become methodology, because its parent is itself unresolved and nothing can be inherited. It becomes an honest question instead of a confident wrong answer. The removal trades a wrong label for a review task, which is the correct direction but raises the count rather than lowering it.

structural_rule_version becomes "2.4". A keyword change alters what gets stored, so it earns a number by the same test 2.2 set: the version exists so a reader of stored data knows which rules produced it, and that includes the keyword set.
No rule, container or structural change. Reference fixture unchanged.

Still open from the same four-paper test and NOT changed here: "measurement" under methodology (mislabelled a Discussion subsection), and the no-H1 case where a paper's title classifies as an ordinary section. Both need a decision rather than a keyword edit.

methodology.note: Includes flattened method-subsection and validity-check keywords (no subroles exist at MVP).

results.note: Includes flattened robustness/replication keywords and former qualitative_findings keywords. A bare 'Findings' heading matches this single role (one distinct role) and resolves by rule.

author_contributions.note: 'credit authorship contribution statement' added per G2 alias set (CRediT convention).

data_availability.note: Skipped for claim extraction, but actively read by the Reporting Compliance Agent's Tier 1 disclosure check. Distinct from administrative content, which nothing downstream currently consumes.

ethics_statement.note: Same reasoning as data_availability -- consumed by the Reporting Compliance Agent, not genuinely unused.

conflict_of_interest.note: Singular 'competing interest' and 'declaration of competing interest(s)' variants added per G2 alias set (Elsevier convention).

appendix.parse_rule: If the normalized heading begins with a trigger: structural_container = appendix; an immediately following short token ('B', '1', 'A1') is captured as appendix_label; any remaining text after separator (':' '.' '-') becomes semantic_heading and is classified normally through the role table. If the heading is only the trigger (+ optional label), or matches an alias exactly: semantic_heading = null.
appendix.bare_container_behavior: semantic_heading = null -> primary_role = Unknown, content_class = analytical, classification_status = resolved, classification_method = structural, NO ReviewTask. Children classify independently.
appendix.unmatched_suffix_behavior: semantic_heading is present but matches 0 roles -> primary_role = Unknown, content_class = analytical, classification_status = resolved, classification_method = structural, NO ReviewTask. semantic_heading is RETAINED. Before 2.2 this raised zero_role_match, which meant adding unparseable words to a bare 'Appendix B' turned a resolved answer into an unresolved one -- backwards, since the extra words carry no epistemic claim to adjudicate. A suffix that DOES match keeps its role: 'Appendix B: Robustness checks' is still results (rule).

examples.appendix a - isolating extended supply c: container=appendix, label=A, semantic_heading='isolating extended supply chains' matches no role -> primary_role=Unknown (structural), no ReviewTask

appendix.note: Appendix answers WHERE content is located; roles answer WHAT epistemic function content performs. Appendix therefore does not compete as a primary_role.

unknown.assigned_when: (a) no headings exist in the document at all -- single whole-document node; (b) a structural container heading has no semantic suffix (bare 'Appendix B', or a container alias like 'Supporting information'); or (c) as of 2.2, a structural container heading whose semantic suffix matches no role
unknown.note: Deliberate assignments (classification_status = resolved, method = structural), NOT classification failures, and generate no ReviewTask. Ordinary zero-match or multi-role headings still do NOT receive Unknown: they get primary_role = null, unresolved, and a ReviewTask -- unless 2.2 inheritance resolves them from a parent, which records method = inherited and a real role, never Unknown.

document_title.note: node_kind, deliberately NOT a section role. primary_role = null, content_class = administrative, classification_method = structural. Only the first H1 can be the title candidate; identification rules and run-level title fields are in spec sections 4 and 8.

section.note: Every other node, including non-first H1s (anomalous, classified deterministically like any node).
